I’m sorry to hear you’re seeing a £300 bill from Vercel—that certainly sounds unexpected. Let’s walk through a few common reasons why a bill could pop up even if you’ve normally been on the free tier, and then some next‑steps you can take. --- ## 1. **What Can Trigger a Charge?** | Category | Typical Triggers | Why it Might Look “free” at first glance | |----------|------------------|----------------------------------------| | **Deployments** | Exceeding the free limits on **build minutes** or **build bandwidth**. | You might have a very active site (daily deploys, CI/CD integrations) that use up minutes rapidly. | | **Serverless Functions** | High number of invocations or execution time beyond free quotas. | Some functions run in the background or on every page load; you might not realize how often they fire. | | **Large Static Assets** | Hosting large assets (e.g., hundreds of MB of images, PDFs, video) that exceed the free bandwidth allowance. | Bulk uploads or having many branches with the same assets can add up. | | **Analytics & Log Retention** | Storing many logs or keeping a long history. | Vercel’s free plan offers limited log retention; moving to a paid plan expands that. | | **Team or Enterprise Features** | Adding team members, new “Pro” or “Enterprise” features, or enabling advanced integrations. | Even a single paid feature can shift the billing model. | | **Custom Domains** | Some domain registrars and TLS certificates can incur costs. | Rarely, Vercel pays for certain certificate authorities, which can appear on your bill. | --- ## 2. **How to Identify the Exact Charge** ### a. Go to **Vercel Dashboard → Billing** 1. Open Vercel. 2. Click **‘Account’** (top‑right). 3. Select **‘Billing’**. You’ll see a summary and a breakdown of charges over the past 30 days (or the billing period). Look for: - A “**Builds**” or “**Functions**” line item with a large number. - Any “**Feature X**” that isn’t on your free plan. ### b. Check **Deployments & Build Usage** - **Deploy History** tab – count the number of builds in the period. - Each build will show the **minutes** used. Sum them up; Vercel often lists the total minutes spent. ### c. Inspect **Serverless Function Metrics** - In **Project → Settings → Functions** you can view logs for the past *X* days. - Quantify how many invocations each function is getting. ### d. Review **Team & Subscription Settings** - A “Member added” event will trigger a cost if the added member has a paid role. - In **Settings → Teams** see if the plan changed from **Hobby/FREE** to **Pro** or **Enterprise**. --- ## 3. **Common “Surprise” Scenarios** 1. **GitHub (or GitLab) Pushes** Each push can trigger a deployment. Pushes to many branches (esp. if you use GitHub Actions to deploy on every push) can quickly climb minutes. 2. **Large Build Artifacts** If you’re building a big monorepo or bundling heavy assets, the build output can grow large and lead to high **build bandwidth** charges. 3. **Using the “Preview” Function** Vercel’s preview deployments are free, but if you have many feature branches or a long‑lived preview, the cost can add up. 4. **Third‑Party Integrations** Some integrations (like a CMS or analytics) may trigger paid usage of Vercel’s backend services. 5. **Unexpected Traffic** A sudden spike in traffic (e.g., a viral post or a bot attack) can cause many serverless function invocations. --- ## 4. **What To Do Now?** | Step | What to do | How it helps | |------|------------|--------------| | **1. Pinpoint the Charge** | Use the Billing → Invoice details to see exact line items. | You’ll know which service is costing you. | | **2. Review Your Usage** | Check Deploy History and Functions metrics. | Spot any abnormal patterns. | | **3. Adjust Your Plan** | If you are over the free tier, decide if you need a paid plan or can reduce usage. | Prevent future surprises. | | **4. Contact Vercel Support** | Reach out via the dashboard or email support@vercel.com with your invoice number. | They can often provide a breakdown or refund if something went wrong. | | **5. Set Up Alerts** | Vercel now allows **usage alerts**. Set a threshold (e.g., 100 build minutes) so you get notified before hitting a bill. | Helps catch spikes early. | | **6. Optimize** | - **Throttle deploys**: deploy only from main or staging.
- **Cache** heavy assets.
- **Split functions**: Move heavy functions to a dedicated server or use on‑demand providers like **Vercel Edge Functions**. | Keeps usage within free limits. | --- ## 5. Quick Fixes to Cut Down Costs | Issue | Quick Fix | |--------|-----------| | **Too many build minutes** | Use [Vercel’s Build Optimization](https://vercel.com/docs/build-init) & cache `node_modules`. | | **Function invocations** | Combine small functions; use **Edge Functions** (free up to a limit). | | **Large assets** | Move large files to a separate CDN or static host (e.g., Cloudflare R2, Netlify Large Media). | | **Unnecessary Domains** | Remove unused custom domains or certificates. | | **Team license on free account** | Make sure your account is set to “Hobby” if you don’t need Pro features. | --- ## 6. Bottom Line - **A £300 bill** likely means you pushed over a free‑tier threshold (deploy minutes, function invocations, or added a paid feature). - Open the **Billing** section to see the exact cause. - Either scale back, switch to a paid plan that matches your usage, or correct the trigger (e.g., fewer deploys). - Use alerts and monitoring to avoid future surprises. If you still can’t locate where the charge came from, reach out to Vercel support right away—the sooner you do, the quicker they can investigate and potentially reverse a mistake. Let me know if you’d like a deeper dive into any step or help setting up usage alerts!
